C-BROWSER-DOWNLOADS-COOKIES-REALITY-REME.Summary:
Superseding remediation for the M1.3 downloads/cookies slice and the browser-provider prerequisites whose current implementation invalidates production evidence.
This change replaces simulated/reference-only proof with a genuine production browser path, integrates completed download artifacts with the generic host blob authority model, fixes cookie-domain authorization, repairs persistence and GRACE projections, and restores fail-closed hosted evidence.
It supersedes the implementation claims of C-BROWSER-DOWNLOADS-COOKIES-SERVICES-20260901 where those claims depended on ReferenceBrowserBackend, InMemoryCookieEngine, local ArtifactStore or premature GRACE apply state.
The archived predecessor remains historical evidence and is not silently rewritten into success.
C-BROWSER-DOWNLOADS-COOKIES-REALITY-REME.Problem:
The predecessor M1.3 slice was marked applied before required hosted evidence was green and several acceptance claims are not backed by the production execution path.
CefBrowserBackend currently delegates browser operations to ReferenceBrowserBackend.
worldline-browser-provider-process parses a backend selector but unconditionally constructs ReferenceBrowserBackend.
S3B constructs BrowserProviderCore directly with ReferenceBrowserBackend, manually injects download lifecycle callbacks and uses InMemoryCookieEngine.
The downloads ArtifactStore is a process-local in-memory map rather than the generic host blob boundary and therefore cannot prove independent blob-read authority or durable artifact ownership.
ArtifactRef.sha256_hash is populated by a non-SHA-256 hash.
Cookie domain filtering uses raw string suffix matching and therefore does not satisfy host/domain authorization semantics.
ClearStorageResponse currently reports success independently of actual storage outcome.
GRACE graph/verification projections contain browser-service module data that is not correctly indexed, and the local workspace may contain an overlapping active predecessor bundle.
The current implementation therefore cannot honestly satisfy the production, security, persistence or hosted-evidence claims required for the M1.3 downloads/cookies slice.

Goals.Goal: Establish one real production browser-provider execution path selected explicitly by the native provider process and backed by CefBrowserBackend rather than ReferenceBrowserBackend.
Remove ReferenceBrowserBackend from the production CEF implementation path except where explicitly retained as a test/reference fixture.
Make the native provider --backend selection authoritative, validated and fail-closed for unknown or unavailable production backends.
Route engine cookie, storage and download operations used by S3B through the real native plugin/provider boundary.
Replace the downloads-local ArtifactStore as production evidence with the generic M1.2 blob/artifact host mechanism and normal broker authority.
Prove download metadata authority and artifact-content-read authority are independently granted.
Use actual SHA-256 where the public contract says sha256_hash.
Implement canonical cookie host/domain matching with label boundaries and explicit host-only/domain-cookie semantics.
Repair site-data result semantics and add hostile cross-domain tests.
Repair GRACE graph/verification projections and remove overlapping active predecessor state before final verification.
Produce fresh local and hosted evidence before this remediation can be applied.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL AND EXACT PLAN APPROVAL ARE SEPARATE. THIS DRAFT DOES NOT AUTHORIZE IMPLEMENTATION.
DO NOT EDIT THE ARCHIVED PREDECESSOR TO PRETEND ITS ORIGINAL HOSTED RUN WAS GREEN.

ANY ACTIVE COPY OF C-BROWSER-DOWNLOADS-COOKIES-SERVICES-20260901 THAT CONFLICTS WITH ITS ARCHIVED INSTANCE MUST BE RESOLVED THROUGH THE NORMAL GRACE LIFECYCLE BEFORE THIS REMEDIATION PLAN IS EXECUTED.
PRODUCTION CEF CODE MUST NOT DELEGATE BROWSER SEMANTICS TO ReferenceBrowserBackend.
ReferenceBrowserBackend MAY REMAIN AVAILABLE ONLY FOR UNIT, CONTRACT, DETERMINISTIC REFERENCE AND EXPLICIT NON-PRODUCTION TEST PATHS.
THE NATIVE PROVIDER PROCESS MUST NOT SILENTLY FALL BACK FROM REQUESTED CEF/PRODUCTION BACKEND TO REFERENCE.
UNKNOWN BACKEND, MISSING REQUIRED CEF ASSETS OR CEF INITIALIZATION FAILURE MUST PRODUCE AN ACTIONABLE STARTUP/HEALTH FAILURE.
CEF TYPES, POINTERS, CALLBACK OBJECTS AND PLATFORM HANDLES MUST NOT CROSS THE ENGINE-NEUTRAL WORLDLINE CONTRACT OR IPC BOUNDARY.
NO NEW BROWSER-SPECIFIC PRIVILEGED KERNEL PATH IS ALLOWED.
THE GENERIC HOST BLOB MECHANISM REMAINS GENERIC. DO NOT ADD A DOWNLOAD-SPECIFIC KERNEL BLOB STORE.
ArtifactRef IS IDENTITY/METADATA ONLY. POSSESSION OF ArtifactRef DOES NOT GRANT CONTENT READ AUTHORITY.
BLOB READS MUST PASS THROUGH NORMAL PRINCIPAL/CAPABILITY ADMISSION.

IF THE EXISTING EXPERIMENTAL 0.1 GENERIC BLOB API CANNOT EXPRESS BROKERED ARTIFACT READS WITH INDEPENDENT PRINCIPAL AUTHORITY, AN ADDITIVE EXPERIMENTAL 0.2 OR SEPARATELY NAMED NEW EXPERIMENTAL CONTRACT IS PERMITTED. IT MUST PRESERVE 0.1 CONTRACTS, FIXTURES AND COMPATIBILITY TESTS; IT MUST NOT REINTERPRET, REMOVE OR WEAKEN 0.1 IN PLACE.
COMPLETED DOWNLOAD ARTIFACTS REQUIRED TO SURVIVE SERVICE RESTART MUST NOT DEPEND SOLELY ON PROCESS-LOCAL MEMORY.
sha256_hash MUST CONTAIN SHA-256 OR THE CONTRACT FIELD MUST BE REPLACED BY A CORRECTLY VERSIONED GENERIC DIGEST REPRESENTATION. DO NOT LABEL FNV OR ANOTHER HASH AS SHA-256.
COOKIE AUTHORIZATION MUST NOT USE raw ends_with(domain) OR EQUIVALENT STRING-SUFFIX MATCHING.
COOKIE MATCHING MUST CANONICALIZE HOSTS AND ENFORCE DNS LABEL BOUNDARIES.
HOST-ONLY COOKIE AND DOMAIN COOKIE SEMANTICS MUST BE EXPLICIT AND TESTED.

IF THE EXISTING EXPERIMENTAL 0.1 COOKIE PRIMITIVE CANNOT EXPRESS THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN HOST-ONLY AND DOMAIN COOKIES, AN ADDITIVE EXPERIMENTAL 0.2 OR SEPARATELY NAMED NEW EXPERIMENTAL CONTRACT IS PERMITTED. IT MUST PRESERVE 0.1 CONTRACTS, FIXTURES AND COMPATIBILITY TESTS; IT MUST NOT SILENTLY REINTERPRET OR BREAK 0.1 SEMANTICS.
INVALID, PRIVILEGED OR NON-HOST COOKIE TARGETS MUST FAIL CLOSED.
BrowserContextId REMAINS PART OF THE AUTHORITATIVE COOKIE/STORAGE SCOPE; EQUAL HOSTNAMES DO NOT PERMIT CROSS-CONTEXT ACCESS.
RAW COOKIE VALUES MUST NOT ENTER GENERIC LOGGING, METRICS, TRAJECTORY OR ORDINARY ERROR TEXT.
ClearSiteDataResponse MUST REPRESENT DEFINED OPERATION SEMANTICS RATHER THAN A CONSTANT SUCCESS EXPRESSION.

S3B PRODUCTION EVIDENCE MUST NOT DIRECTLY CONSTRUCT BrowserProviderCore, CALL SERVICE ENGINE CALLBACKS MANUALLY AS THE SOLE ENGINE EVIDENCE, OR USE InMemoryCookieEngine AS THE PRODUCTION COOKIE PROOF.
REFERENCE/IN-MEMORY TESTS MAY REMAIN AS FAST DETERMINISTIC LOWER-LEVEL TESTS BUT MUST BE LABELLED AS SUCH.
EXISTING M0, M1.1, M1.2, S2, S3A AND BROWSER CONTRACT COMPATIBILITY TESTS MUST NOT BE WEAKENED OR SKIPPED.
ALL REQUIRED HOSTED TESTS REMAIN FAIL-CLOSED.

GRACE LINT IS REQUIRED AS A LIFECYCLE PREFLIGHT: RUN grace lint --path . --assertions current BEFORE OBSERVED WRITES, AND RUN THE PLAN-SELECTED FINAL ASSERTION PROFILE BEFORE COMPLETION. IT IS NOT PRODUCT OR RUNTIME ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE AND MUST NOT APPEAR IN VerificationIntent.
THIS REMEDIATION MUST NOT BE TRANSITIONED TO applied OR ARCHIVED AS SUCCESSFULLY APPLIED UNTIL REQUIRED HOSTED EVIDENCE IS GREEN AND EXPLICIT OWNER APPLY CONFIRMATION IS OBTAINED.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Promoting experimental M1.3 contracts to stable v1.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: CefBrowserBackend no longer stores or delegates production browser operations to ReferenceBrowserBackend.
The CEF adapter implements or delegates to genuine CEF-backed context/page/navigation/observe/query/act/download/cookie/storage operations required by the production proving path.
Operations not genuinely implemented by the production CEF backend fail explicitly as Unsupported/Unavailable rather than succeeding through a reference fallback.
worldline-browser-provider-process selects the requested backend through an explicit backend factory or equivalent bounded construction seam.
--backend reference selects ReferenceBrowserBackend only when explicitly requested for reference/test use.
--backend cef selects CefBrowserBackend and a test proves the process cannot silently instantiate ReferenceBrowserBackend instead.
Unknown --backend values fail startup with non-zero status and actionable diagnostics.
The provider handshake/manifest truthfully reports only operations supported by the selected backend.
Production S3B communicates with the browser provider through the normal native plugin IPC/capability path rather than direct BrowserProviderCore construction.
Production S3B creates real browser contexts/pages through the selected CEF-backed provider and uses real engine cookie/storage primitives.
A deterministic loopback download reaches the downloads service through the real engine/provider integration rather than only manual on_engine_download_started/on_engine_download_completed calls.
Manual callback injection remains permitted only in separately named unit/reference tests.
Completed download bytes are inserted through the existing generic host blob protocol/storage path or an explicitly generic additive completion of that path.
worldline-browser-downloads does not use an in-memory BTreeMap as the authoritative production artifact store.
Artifact metadata persists sufficiently for a completed download record to remain valid across downloads-service restart.
A principal with browser.downloads.read can inspect DownloadRecord and ArtifactRef metadata but receives AccessDenied when attempting blob bytes without the separate generic blob-read grant.
A principal with the admitted generic blob-read grant can read the same artifact through the normal broker/host boundary.
Cross-principal or cross-scope blob access is rejected even when the attacker knows the opaque artifact identifier.

The implementation documents whether experimental 0.1 can provide brokered artifact reads with independent authority. If it cannot, the contract delta is additive experimental 0.2 or a new experimental contract, while 0.1 fixtures and compatibility tests remain intact.
Artifact content digest is actual SHA-256 and verified against deterministic fixture bytes.
Cookie domain matching uses canonicalized host/domain semantics and DNS label boundaries.
example.com domain-cookie matching accepts an authorized sub.example.com case according to the documented model.
evil-example.com does not match example.com.
Case normalization is tested.
Trailing-dot/canonical-host behavior is explicitly defined and tested.
Invalid empty hosts, malformed domains and unsupported scheme targets fail closed.
Host-only cookies do not become domain cookies by normalization.

The implementation documents whether experimental 0.1 can represent host-only and domain-cookie distinction. If it cannot, the contract delta is additive experimental 0.2 or a new experimental contract, while 0.1 fixtures and compatibility tests remain intact.
Context A cannot enumerate, read, mutate or delete Context B cookie data for the same canonical host.
Cookie value DTO debug/diagnostic representation remains redacted.
ClearSiteDataResponse has documented deterministic semantics and no constant `... || true` implementation remains.
Site-data clearing against Context A/origin X cannot clear Context B or a sibling origin.
Download uncertain-outcome reconciliation still does not automatically replay a potentially completed start.
Existing compile failure around EngineDownloadStartedEvent or its replacement is resolved through the approved contract design rather than by leaving an undefined test-only type.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings is green without broad lint suppression for the newly introduced errors.
.grace/graph/index.xml owns every browser-service graph module present in the indexed graph document, including M-BROWSER-SERVICE-PLUGINS where applicable.
.grace/verification/index.xml owns the corresponding verification module, including V-M-BROWSER-SERVICE-PLUGINS where applicable.
No duplicate active/archive change identity remains for C-BROWSER-DOWNLOADS-COOKIES-SERVICES-20260901.
The predecessor remains historically recorded as the superseded flawed slice rather than being retroactively presented as having passed hosted CI.

A dedicated real S3B hosted Windows job proves: production CEF provider selection, native IPC, real engine cookie/storage operations, real download integration, generic blob authority separation, service restart, and context isolation.
Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, ProvingSlice, RealChromium, BrowserProvider, BrowserServices and the real S3B required hosted gate are all green for the same remediation commit.
Local completion evidence and hosted completion evidence are reported separately.
Completion packet explicitly lists the prior red hosted run and the new green superseding run.
This remediation is neither transitioned to applied nor archived as successfully applied until required hosted evidence is green and an owner explicitly confirms apply.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh evidence distinguishes reference/unit tests from production tests and demonstrates a real CEF-selected native provider path, real cookie/storage/download engine integration, generic brokered blob access, SHA-256 artifact verification, hostile cookie-domain cases, persistence and restart behavior, repaired GRACE projections, no duplicate active predecessor, clippy-clean source and a fresh required hosted run.

Assumptions.Assumption: The current production-provider claims are considered unproven until this remediation produces fresh evidence; previously green reference-backed tests remain useful but are not promoted to production evidence.
Existing M0.6 generic native IPC and M1.2 generic blob protocol are the intended mechanisms and should be completed/reused rather than replaced by browser-specific transports.
ReferenceBrowserBackend remains valuable as deterministic reference infrastructure once its production role is removed.
The exact CEF binding implementation strategy is chosen in the separately approved plan after inspecting currently available CEF primitives and thread-affinity requirements.

If the existing CEF wrapper lacks enough real implementation to satisfy the required operations, the plan may explicitly stage those operations inside this remediation rather than pretending the wrapper is already a production backend.
The local duplicate active predecessor described in preflight is workspace state not visible in the remote repository; its exact cleanup must be validated locally by GRACE before execution.
Request-policy/adblock and later M1.3 slices remain blocked until this remediation is applied.
